- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral/uncertain), model tends to err on the side of overreaction; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% for next 7 days.
